runners_data.name: Emerald Bay
runners_data.note: Ran on debut and in sellers at 5-6f, now stepping up to 7½f for trainer George Scott; a genuine hold-up type that the pace map has shifted into a midfield position simply because true backmarkers are oversubscribed in this five-runner field — P J McDonald takes the ride with the tongue tie applied, and the step up in trip on good to firm is the key unknown.|

runners_data.name: Farndale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up filly has three runs at 7f+ without threatening the frame, but good-ground form and a consistent trip profile mean the conditions suit her style; Sean Kirrane is a competent northern claimer but the lack of any win or placed finish makes improvement the only route to relevance here.|

runners_data.name: Amantha
runners_data.note: Boasts the highest OR in the field at 59 and landed a win over 7f on good ground most recently — the drop to nursery company at Beverley on similar going is a positive angle for Brian Ellison's filly; Pierre-Louis Jamin rode the winning race and retains the ride, and with the best recent form figure (1 in her last five) she is the most obvious class horse in the race.|

runners_data.name: Tiger In The Tree
runners_data.note: The lone front runner in this field, giving Duran Fentiman an uncomplicated lead if he wants it; the horse is tagged as fading in the finish and its form figures of 9-6-9 are modest, but Tim Easterby's 14-day strike rate of 8/104 and the uncontested pace make this a more interesting prospect than the bare OR of 51 suggests — racing in role is the key asset.|

runners_data.name: Happy Humpo
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon picks up the mount for Charlie Clover (no winners in the last 14 days from six runners), and Happy Humpo is a natural hold-up horse by style mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; the horse fades in the finish, has a poor going record on similar ground (1/3 comparable), and the lowest OR in the field at 46 makes this a tough assignment.|

races.paceDynamic: Tiger In The Tree is the sole confirmed front runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to press for the lead, is set to dictate a sustainable gallop from the front over 7½f at Beverley on good to firm ground. With just five runners and a lone pace-setter, the tempo will be controlled and measured — Tiger In The Tree can set the fractions to suit, potentially stealing a march on the field around the final turn. The absence of any rival willing or able to aggressively dispute the lead means closers face a tactical challenge, as the pace may not be fierce enough to reel in a horse that travels kindly in front. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up/staying-on profiles that can produce a sustained late run over this stiff 7½f track, provided the pace is honest enough — but if Tiger In The Tree rolls along at a canter, horses with the class and tactical acumen to sit just off the pace and quicken are better placed than pure backmarkers. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo are genuine hold-up horses shuffled into the midfield depiction because there is simply no room for all of them at the back; in a five-runner field, Amantha and Farndale are most likely to fill the midfield-to-rear positions naturally.

scenarios.body: If the pace is honest enough to stretch the field and a genuine closer produces a sustained late run to swallow up the leader.

scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate

watchPoints.text: Tiger In The Tree is the only confirmed front runner and Duran Fentiman could dictate every fraction — watch whether it is allowed to bowl along unchallenged, as a crawl in front is a serious winning threat even for a horse with modest form figures.

Amantha is the highest-rated runner and won over 7f on good ground last time; watch how Pierre-Louis Jamin positions her from the gate — if she gets a prominent enough pitch she could hit the line too strongly for the leader.

Emerald Bay and Happy Humpo are both natural backmarkers mapped to midfield in the pace diagram; in a five-runner field they may find themselves further back than ideal, meaning their finishing efforts depend entirely on the pace being genuinely honest.

The going is reported as Good to Firm across all Beverley races today — this is faster than the declared Good and could expose any runner with a concern on quick ground, particularly those whose previous form has come on softer surfaces such as Happy Humpo (1/3 on comparable going).
Both Beverley 7½f Nurseries on the card share similar going conditions — compare splits from the earlier 2:52 race to assess whether the pace up front is truly honest before the 3:24 field returns.

races.name: Charlie Wood Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Al Aasy
runners_data.note: Veteran nine-year-old for William Haggas who is the lone confirmed pace-setter here; Good to Firm is within his comfort zone (10 runs, 3 wins on similar ground) and Cieren Fallon can dictate terms, though a 77-day absence and a style-fit flag for racing outside his natural role tempers enthusiasm slightly.

runners_data.name: By The Book
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's five-year-old arrives 98 days since last run and holds Listed/Group form at 12-14f — a natural prominent racer who will be squeezed for his preferred early position by multiple rivals of similar style, making a clean passage from the front not guaranteed; his form at 12f on Good (3rd, 1st, 3rd) is solid.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's charge is freshest of the prominent trio at just 27 days since last run, and the step up to 1m4f from his recent 10f outings looks interesting; like By The Book he carries front-running instincts that will be frustrated by a congested early position battle, so his chance depends on finding a clean berth close to Al Aasy.

runners_data.name: Miss Wong
runners_data.note: David Simcock's four-year-old is the only genuine hold-up horse in the field, wearing a hood, and her record shows she operates best when given a strong pace to chase — a controlled, steady gallop set by an uncontested leader is not her ideal scenario, and six recent efforts over 12-14f without a win on Good suggest she needs things to go right.

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is in good heart (won 11 days ago at 10f on Good) and races prominently by nature, though in this company she has been pushed back to a midfield mapping because the field is stacked with similar types ahead of her; drop back to 12f suits, but this Listed class is a significant hike from what she has faced.

runners_data.name: Phantom Flight
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — George Scott's seven-year-old does not take part, so his strong Good-ground profile (14 runs, 4 wins on similar) is irrelevant to this race's shape and outcome.

races.paceDynamic: Al Aasy is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control this 1m4f contest from the front at a pace entirely of Cieren Fallon's choosing on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. That uncontested lead almost certainly translates into a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a searching test — a shape that rewards those who can travel comfortably in behind and quicken off that tempo, but most critically suits the leader if he settles well and pings the bend. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: By The Book, Involvement, and Percy's Daydream are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who will be jostling for early positions they cannot all claim, with By The Book (Charlie Appleby, higher OR) and Involvement (recent run 27 days ago, freshest of the trio) the most likely to secure a place close to Al Aasy. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested pace set by a single front-runner — strongly favours the horse on the front end or the closest prominent tracker who can quicken off a steady clip, rather than genuine hold-up types coming from behind.

scenarios.title: Al Aasy Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Al Aasy is allowed to dictate an uncontested, even gallop and conserves enough to kick again entering the straight.
scenarios.body: If Al Aasy is allowed to dictate an uncontested, even gallop and conserves enough to kick again entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just too steady and a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to outfinish Al Aasy in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is just too steady and a prominent tracker conserves enough energy to outfinish Al Aasy in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is misjudged upwards and the field strings out, allowing a hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is misjudged upwards and the field strings out, allowing a hold-up horse to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Front Two Fall Short
scenarios.trigger: If the field overheats early and multiple prominent types burn out, leaving the race open for a fresh closer or an outsider to capitalise.
scenarios.body: If the field overheats early and multiple prominent types burn out, leaving the race open for a fresh closer or an outsider to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Al Aasy's uncontested lead is the fulcrum of this race — if Cieren Fallon dictates a truly slow early pace the race could compress dramatically in the final two furlongs and expose any horse who switches off.

By The Book, Involvement, and Percy's Daydream are all natural prominent types competing for the same early positions — watch for crowding and bumping leaving the stalls or through the first two furlongs as they jostle for the one available tracking slot.

Miss Wong's hood and hold-up style make her entirely dependent on the pace being genuine; if Al Aasy crawls, she has no race to run into and Connor Beasley will face an impossible task timing a challenge.

Beverley's 1m4f is effectively flat but the track's unique straight finish can expose horses who are pulled wide on the turn — worth watching how the prominent pack fans out approaching the home straight given the traffic scenario in midfield.

Percy's Daydream won just 11 days ago and races here at Listed level for the first time — watch early to see whether Mark Winn attempts to push forward to claim a prominent spot or accepts a midfield berth, as that decision will shape her chance entirely.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Coconut Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo for Marco Botti who has won two of her last three starts, both at 8f on Standard; PJ McDonald aboard adds significant jockey quality, and her prominent style suits this race shape ideally — she is the most likely immediate beneficiary if Porth Eilian sets a comfortable pace.

runners_data.name: Enamorus
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply in trip from recent 7f efforts and that distance question is the primary concern; Oisin Orr rides but her recent form shows a drop-off, and she lacks the pace profile to naturally attack this race shape from the front, likely finding herself in mid-to-rear with a lot to do.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Dylan Cunha who ran just nine days ago — bounce factor worth noting — but her repeated placed efforts on Good and Good to Soft suggest she handles the going; needs a stronger-than-expected pace to produce her best, which this race may not provide.

runners_data.name: Cancelled
runners_data.note: Oldest horse in the field at five and wearing a tongue piece; ran 48 days ago and trips from 9-10f are her natural home, so 1m½f is on the sharp side — her hold-up style is authentic but the distance and layoff are both mild negatives in a race likely run at a controlled tempo.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who won over 8f on Standard earlier in the year but has not reproduced that form on turf; tongue tie noted, and while Zak Wheatley rides, her hold-up style needs a strongly run race to unlock her — the controlled pace scenario makes her unlikely to get involved at the business end.

runners_data.name: Porth Eilian
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed lead-setter and one whose style fits this track and trip well; she has won over 8f at Beverley and is likely to go uncontested to the front, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a mild reminder that if the race shape shifts she has limited fallback — her chance is heavily dependent on leading and controlling the fractions.

runners_data.name: Sandy Craic
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good for David O'Meara and has shown consistent placed form at sprint-to-mile trips; a natural prominent type who should slot in just off Porth Eilian's shoulder, and that position could prove ideal if the leader fades late in the straight.

runners_data.name: Sogniamo
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on Good and drops back to 1m½f here, which is worth monitoring given that recent win came at a longer trip; prominent style suits the race shape and O'Meara's second string is interesting, but Mark Winn's booking (rather than Hart) suggests stable pecking order is with Sandy Craic.

runners_data.name: Vitality
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural position is just behind the leader, but with Sandy Craic, Sogniamo, and Lexington Express all competing for the same ground, she is likely to be squeezed back further than ideal; the STYLE_FIT (0.90) and redistribution both temper her prospects unless the pace scenario unexpectedly opens up.

runners_data.name: Ma Leila
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for Tom Clover with only three runs to her name; bumped into prominent company and unlikely to secure her natural pressing role here given the competition for early positions — Ryan Sexton takes over in the saddle and she will need the race to come to her from an uncharacteristic position.

races.paceDynamic: Porth Eilian is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival of equivalent lead-bias in this field, she is likely to coast into a comfortable early lead at a pace she controls entirely on Good to Firm ground over 1m½f at Beverley. Sandy Craic, Sogniamo, and Lexington Express will press forward into the prominent positions just behind her, creating a structured but not savage gallop — the kind of tempo that rewards those who travel well and strike early in the straight rather than those who need a true test. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically hold their natural position: Vitality and Ma Leila are genuine prominent racers but are mapped to midfield, with Sandy Craic and Sogniamo the likelier occupants of the places directly behind Porth Eilian. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead at a sustainable pace on fast ground — most strongly favours prominent-to-mid-field types who can travel close to the pace and pounce in the home straight without needing a stamina-sapping gallop to bring them into it.

scenarios.body: If the early pace proves too slow and the race turns into a sprint finish that brings hold-up runners into play.

scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Porth Eilian, untroubled on a sound surface she handles well, simply stretches clear and is never reeled in.

watchPoints.text: Porth Eilian — if she is allowed to bowl along entirely uncontested through the first half-mile, monitor whether any of Sandy Craic or Sogniamo close the gap approaching the home turn, as her lead may prove unassailable if they sit too far off her.

Sogniamo — drops from 9f to 1m½f having won at the longer trip; watch the market move to gauge whether O'Meara views this as a sharp enough test, because a pace that does not truly stretch her could leave her running on empty in the final furlong.

Come On Eibhlin — ran only nine days ago and returns quickly; if she shows any signs of sluggishness in the early exchanges her hold-up position becomes a liability rather than a weapon in a race not likely to be run at a true gallop.

Vitality and Ma Leila — both genuine prominent types who are likely to be shuffled back from their natural racing position by the volume of early-pace horses; watch whether either jockey attempts to push forward regardless, as that decision could cause significant bunching in the first two furlongs and disrupt the race shape entirely.

races.name: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap

runners_data.name: Capital Guarantee
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up specialist has sound form on similar going (one win and three places from 15 runs) but a string of double-figure finishes recently raises questions about consistency, and 21 days since last run is not a concern; this race shape, with a steady pace, may not generate the strong end-to-end gallop needed to bring a pure closer home in time.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's five-year-old carries strong recent form — two wins from eight runs on similar going — and is a natural prominent type who should travel comfortably in second or third, making him well-suited to a race where the front two or three are likely to fight it out; only 12 days since last run is fine, and Alistair Rawlinson is a competent claimer at this level.

runners_data.name: Degale
runners_data.note: David and Nicola Barron's gelding is genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination, though the crowded rear of this field means he will realistically be forced to race closer to midfield than he prefers; form figures of 603050 are modest, and a STYLE_FIT flag means his chance should be tempered if he cannot settle into his natural rhythm.

runners_data.name: It Just Takes Time
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's veteran is the confirmed pace-setter in this race and recent efforts show two seconds on identical going over 7f, giving confidence he will travel well to the front; at eight years old and top weight on 135lbs, the concern is whether he can sustain that effort up Beverley's stiff finish if Tattie Bogle or Coolree press him, and the STYLE_FIT tag is more about the field dynamic than his role here.

runners_data.name: Glenfinnan
runners_data.note: Michael Dods's six-year-old is a hold-up type (headgear noted) with one win on similar ground in recent history, and his best form has come when a strong pace has been set allowing him to close; 10 days since last run is not an issue, but this pace scenario — moderate rather than strong — may not fully bring him into contention late enough over 7½f at Beverley.

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old is arguably the most interesting runner here — prominent in style, in excellent recent form (two wins and three places from last five including two seconds on good ground over identical 7f trips), and only three days since last run suggests a trainer confident of a quick turnaround; she should be competing for second or third on the rail and her weight of 128lbs is competitive.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Sam England's seven-year-old wears a tongue-tie and is a naturally forward-going horse, but in a field this rich in prominent types he is unlikely to secure the front rank he ideally wants; his form shows wins on good-to-soft and good ground at 8f, and the slight drop in class on OR=69 gives him a theoretical chance, but the redistribution away from his preferred front position tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's six-year-old carries a visor and is a genuine hold-up type compressed into a midfield position by the shape of this field; a form string of 046668 and a sim-going record of just one place from 15 runs on similar ground makes it very hard to make a case, and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/4 adds further caution.

races.paceDynamic: It Just Takes Time is the confirmed front-runner and, with only Tattie Bogle and Highland Olly likely to press forward, this shapes up as a race with a manageable, sustainable gallop rather than a pressured affair — on Good to Firm ground at Beverley, that means a decent clip will be set but without genuine pace warfare. It Just Takes Time can dictate from the front, controlling fractions through Beverley's stiff finish, and the absence of a genuine pace rival should allow the leader to conserve enough to fight out the closing stages. This race shape favours horses who can race prominently or within a length or two of the pace, as the lack of a true stamina test over 7½f on fast ground will not necessarily bring the hold-up horses into play late enough. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can realistically secure their natural position — Coolree is a genuine prominent racer who will be competing for a forward berth with It Just Takes Time and Highland Olly, while Degale and Bajan Bandit are true hold-up horses shuffled into a midfield mapping; Tattie Bogle's strong recent form and natural forwardness make her the most likely to lock in a prominent position behind the leader.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time sets a sustainable pace and prominent horses inherit the front rank turning for home, allowing Tattie Bogle or Highland Olly to challenge off the shoulder.
scenarios.body: If It Just Takes Time sets a sustainable pace and prominent horses inherit the front rank turning for home, allowing Tattie Bogle or Highland Olly to challenge off the shoulder.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are slow enough that the race becomes a sprint finish, allowing horses with a turn of foot to close from midfield.
scenarios.body: If the early fractions are slow enough that the race becomes a sprint finish, allowing horses with a turn of foot to close from midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If It Just Takes Time travels well throughout and the pace is genuinely sustainable but not suicidal, enabling the leader to grind out a win up Beverley's stiff finish.
scenarios.body: If It Just Takes Time travels well throughout and the pace is genuinely sustainable but not suicidal, enabling the leader to grind out a win up Beverley's stiff finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the race truly sets up for a late closer, allowing one of the deeper-lying types to pick up ground in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the race truly sets up for a late closer, allowing one of the deeper-lying types to pick up ground in the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Tattie Bogle's three-day turnaround is a bold move by Charlie Johnston — watch whether she comes into the race fresh and travels kindly, as her recent form and style make her the biggest threat to any leader if she secures a prominent pitch.

Coolree will attempt to press forward from stall position but faces It Just Takes Time and Highland Olly for the same ground — watch the first furlong for crowding on the front rank, which could force Coolree to drop back and race out of character.

Glenfinnan's hold-up profile means everything depends on the pace being strong enough to create a gap in the final furlong — if It Just Takes Time controls things at a moderate tempo, Glenfinnan's late run may simply not materialise quickly enough up Beverley's stiff finish.

It Just Takes Time on top weight of 135lbs bears close watching through the final two furlongs — if he begins to idle or roll under pressure after setting the pace, Tattie Bogle or Highland Olly tracking him closely are best placed to capitalise.

Bajan Bandit's visor is worth noting as a first-time or recent application — check if this represents a stable thinking the horse needs a new angle, though the overall profile suggests this is a race to watch rather than to back.

races.name: Happy Birthday Roy Archer Handicap

runners_data.name: Truly Special
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly returning in 26 days, her sole win came over 6f on Soft but she has placed over 7f on Good — the step back from 8f may suit, though her form string (39-661) is modest and she'll need to improve markedly from her recent finishes.|

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter in this race, Cieren Fallon takes over from a horse whose last five runs include four placings, all over 6f on Good or Soft; moving up to 7½f is a query, but an uncontested lead on Good to Firm is a significant asset — her STYLE_FIT flag is a mild discount only if she is somehow not first away.|

runners_data.name: Zoulette
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's hold-up filly has placed twice over 7f on Good ground and arrives 32 days fresh; her form (636726) is uninspiring but she handles the trip and could outrun her mark if the race develops into a test of stamina in the final stages.|

runners_data.name: Forever Twenty
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this genuine closer who naturally wants to come from off the pace, but with several rivals sharing that role he is squeezed into a midfield map position that is not his optimum — his headgear (p) may help him settle, and three placings in seven Good-ground runs give some hope, though an OR of 53 on a declining form line is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's filly (trainer 0-from-5 in 14 days) has not won in eleven visible starts and her best recent effort was a fourth over 7f on Good; her natural closing style will be compromised in a small field running at a controlled pace, and her redistribution to midfield does not truly reflect how she wants to race.|

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent performer has placed in nine of fourteen runs on Good ground including a win over 8f — the drop back to 7½f is no concern — and the hood (b) aids her focus; she is a genuine hold-up operator forced into a midfield map position, but she has the strongest recent placed form of the closers and gives Easterby (7-from-98 in 14 days) his best each-way chance here.|

runners_data.name: Maid On The Shelf
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's filly (9-from-60 in 14 days, Oisin Orr aboard) has only three runs to her name, all over longer trips on Good or Softer ground — stepping down to 7½f may bring her on, and a prominent position just off Battenburg Belle could allow her to maximise a freshness edge after just nine days, though her light experience and wide draw must be respected.|

races.paceDynamic: Battenburg Belle is the lone confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no genuine rivals disputing the lead, she is expected to stride forward under Cieren Fallon and control the tempo throughout the 7½f trip on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. The pace she sets is likely to be measured rather than breakneck — a single leader dictating from the front on fast ground tends to produce a sustainable gallop that keeps the field strung out without burning through the early fractions. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically operate from their natural rear position: Forever Twenty, Walk On Walk On, and Hood Wink are all genuine closers who will be mapped into midfield but may not secure a clean sit-and-deliver trip in behind a lone maker. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested pace with one leader dictating — is likeliest to favour a horse that can track just behind Battenburg Belle in a prominent or handy position and quicken past in the final two furlongs, making Maid On The Shelf and any horse with tactical versatility the primary beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Battenburg Belle's stamina for 7½f is unproven — if she fades after half-mile, the entire race shape collapses and any midfield tracker (Maid On The Shelf, Hood Wink) could inherit the race in a matter of strides.

Hood Wink, Forever Twenty, and Walk On Walk On are all genuine hold-up horses competing in a small field behind a single steady leader — watch for traffic issues and lack of horses to pass if the pace is too conservative.

Maid On The Shelf is lightly raced (only three runs) and untested at this trip — if she fluffs the start or fails to travel prominently under Oisin Orr, her chance in this pace-dependent scenario evaporates quickly.
